title: Jailer 2 Becomes Highest-Grossing Tamil Film Ever at Rs 710 Crore
excerpt: Rajinikanth's sequel passes 2.0 in 11 days, crosses Rs 700 crore worldwide first for Tamil cinema, and adds Rs 64.35 crore in its second weekend in India.
body:
• Jailer 2 has reached Rs 710.35 crore worldwide in 11 days, becoming the highest-grossing Tamil film of all time, according to Sacnilk figures reported by multiple outlets.
  • The Nelson Dilipkumar film surpassed Rajinikanth's own 2.0, which held the record at about Rs 691 crore, and is the first Tamil film to cross Rs 700 crore globally.
  • India net collections stand at Rs 398.70 crore after Day 11, with Rs 64.35 crore coming in the second weekend alone, including Rs 25.70 crore on Sunday, October 25.
  • Rajinikanth joined fans at a theatrical screening for the first time in 40 years, Sun Pictures said, alongside director Nelson and composer Anirudh Ravichander.

Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 has become the highest-grossing Tamil film of all time, reaching Rs 710 crore worldwide in 11 days and passing the record long held by his own 2.0. The milestone, reached on Sunday, October 25, makes the Nelson Dilipkumar sequel the first Tamil film to cross Rs 700 crore globally, according to industry tracker Sacnilk figures reported by The Hollywood Reporter India and Hindustan Times.

The update matters because it is a new record, not a routine daily tally. The Videshi reported earlier on Monday that the film had reached Rs 443 crore in India after its second weekend. The worldwide figure now confirms a different scale: India gross of Rs 466.85 crore plus about Rs 243.50 crore overseas, for a combined Rs 710.35 crore, as detailed by The Cinema Post.

"Passing 2.0, Leo and the First Jailer On Sunday, Jailer 2 surpassed 2.0 's worldwide gross of Rs 691 crore, an eight-year-old record."

A Second Weekend That Lifted the Total

The film had dipped on Friday, then recovered sharply. It earned Rs 14.50 crore in India net on Friday, Rs 24.15 crore on Saturday, and Rs 25.70 crore on Sunday, a combined Rs 64.35 crore for the second weekend. Sunday was its best single day since Wednesday, and the 6.4 percent rise over Saturday showed the run was strengthening rather than fading in week two.

https://x.com/ahimsafilms/status/2114273888473587755

After 11 days, India net stands at Rs 398.70 crore, just Rs 1.30 crore short of Rs 400 crore. Hindustan Times noted the film will become the third Tamil film to reach that domestic mark, after the original Jailer and Vijay's Leo. Overseas, the film has amassed $25.6 million in 11 days, with international earnings on some days matching or exceeding domestic collections.

Passing 2.0, Leo and the First Jailer

On Sunday, Jailer 2 surpassed 2.0's worldwide gross of Rs 691 crore, an eight-year-old record. It had already overtaken its predecessor, at about Rs 604 crore, and Leo, at about Rs 605 crore, on Thursday. The current top five Tamil films worldwide, by Sacnilk lifetime figures cited in coverage, are now led by Jailer 2, followed by 2.0, Leo, Jailer and Coolie at about Rs 518 crore — four of the five starring Rajinikanth.

The film opened on October 15 worldwide. It registered Rs 59 crore in India on opening day and Rs 37 crore on day two, then surged to Rs 47 crore and Rs 55 crore over its first weekend. Globally it took $31.2 million in its three-day opening weekend, rising to $44.5 million over four days across more than 20 markets, and secured the number two spot worldwide that weekend.

Rajinikanth Watches With Fans

Sun Pictures, which produced the film, shared a video of Rajinikanth attending an IMAX show with fans, with Nelson and Anirudh Ravichander. The banner wrote on X: "For the first time in 40 years, Superstar Rajinikanth joins fans to witness #Jailer2 on the big screen!" The appearance underlined the personal nature of the record: the star passing his own previous benchmark, in a sequel he agreed to after previously rejecting sequels to other blockbusters.

Rajinikanth returns as 'Tiger' Muthuvel Pandian. Ramya Krishnan, Yogi Babu, Mirnaa and Rithvik reprise their roles, while S. J. Suryah, Mithun Chakraborty, Suraj Venjaramoodu and Vidya Balan join the cast, with cameos by Mohanlal, Shiva Rajkumar and Jackie Shroff. Anirudh Ravichander composed the music.

What Comes Next

Coverage on Monday pointed to Rs 800 crore and Rs 900 crore as possible next milestones if the current pace holds, after a Sunday worldwide haul of more than Rs 44 crore. The immediate test is the weekday hold and whether India net crosses Rs 400 crore on Monday. For diaspora audiences in North America, the Gulf and Southeast Asia, the overseas share — more than a third of the worldwide total — is the clearest sign of how much of this record was built outside India.
